turns: Good to see you again. You'd planned two things for the week: slow breathing at bedtime and three written lines a night. Tell me how it went.
yeah so i actually kept up with both. wrote my three lines in the notebook every single night and did the breathing right before bed each time.
All seven nights. Did anything change?
sleep did. i was lying awake until like 2 last week, and this week i'm out around midnight. so that's improved for sure.
Good. And what's been weighing on you otherwise?
thursday's stats midterm. i get really anxious about it, like the second i open my notes my stomach just drops.
What's the thought in that moment?
that i'll fail and have to retake the whole class. except this time i noticed it and checked. my grade right now is a b plus, so a single exam isn't going to wreck it. i'm nervous, i'm not doomed.
So you tested the thought. And the nerves, what did you do with those?

tuesday it got bad so i went out for a run, and my head was way clearer after. i also phoned my dad and admitted how stressed i've been, and he was good about it. he told me no grade is worth getting sick over.
How was it to hear that from him?
a relief honestly. grades were always a huge deal with my parents growing up so i didn't expect it.
What do you need between now and Thursday?
a plan. so tomorrow morning two practice sets, wednesday at three i go to office hours, and the night before i quit studying at nine.
That's concrete. Shall the breathing and the three lines continue this week?
yes, both, every night again this week.
Anything you'll take away from today?
just that talking it out helped. it seems a lot more doable than it did when i logged in.
Hello. The plan from last session was the activity worksheet on three separate days. What happened with it?
Nothing happened with it. I never opened the worksheet, let alone filled it in.
I appreciate you saying so plainly. Was something in the way?
Not really, which is the worst part. Everything is just grey. Stuff I used to enjoy doesn't interest me, and I can't work up the energy to care.
Has it been grey for long?
For a while now. It's been three weeks since I started on the antidepressant and so far I notice nothing.
Those can be slow to work. Walk me through a typical day.

I miss the morning lecture because I don't get out of bed, and I promise myself I'll make it up. I never do. There's a paper due that I haven't written a word of, and I keep refusing to even look at it.
That's a lot weighing on you.
Pathetic is what it is. Other people get themselves to class without a problem. I'm the one person who can't hold it together.
You're being very hard on someone who's having a rough time. Could we look at the paper together next session?
I don't know. Maybe. Depends how I'm feeling.
Hello. What do you want to use today for?
The break. I'm going home, and I haven't been to church since September, and I know it's the first thing my parents will bring up. I've been on edge the whole week picturing that dinner.
That does sound stressful. Something that could help: before you travel, write out a list of things you're grateful to your parents for.
Seriously, a gratitude list? That's not what I need at all. I'm not ungrateful. I'm scared of that conversation, and you're not hearing me.
You're right. I reached for a technique instead of listening, and I apologise. The conversation scares you. What are you afraid is going to happen in it?

Thanks. Okay. I picture my mom crying and my dad just going quiet, and both of them concluding that I've tossed out everything they taught me. Which I haven't. Parts of it I still believe. I just can't tell you right now what I believe.
So you're not rejecting them. You're partway through figuring out your own faith, and the fear is that they'll take it as rejection.
Exactly that. Nobody has ever said it to me like that before.
If they could understand one thing, what would you want it to be?
That I'm asking questions. I haven't left.
That's something solid to keep hold of.
Yeah, it is. Once we got to the real issue this actually helped. I'm a little less on edge about going.
Hi. How has your day been so far?
Good. I put kimchi in a grilled cheese at lunch and it might be the best one I've ever made.
So well. The sourness balances out all that cheese. Plain grilled cheese is dead to me now.
Noted. Been doing anything else lately?
I finally started watching that baking contest, the one filmed in a tent that everybody brings up.
Love it. Nothing is ever really at stake. A cake fell apart and the most dramatic consequence was somebody getting hugged.
Right. That's about it from me today though. There's nothing serious happening.

Bad. Monday [REDACTED: NAME] ended it. We were together three years and she did it in the car in about ten minutes. I feel hollowed out, completely gutted, and I can't stop replaying what I might have done differently.
I'm really sorry. To lose that so abruptly is enormous.

The evenings in the apartment are what get me. Her things are still on every shelf and I sit there by myself, lonelier than I have ever been. Most nights I drink so that I don't have to think about any of it.
I appreciate you sharing that. Something you could try is listing your good qualities, as a reminder of how much you would bring to a future partner.
Shall we name three of them now?
No problem. What would be more useful to talk about?
We could simply stay with what the evenings are like.
It's fine. Let's just stop for today.
Sure. Come back whenever you'd like.
Good to have you back. You were going to do the slow breathing each evening, five days running. How did that turn out?
Sort of. Monday and Tuesday I did it, and after that it fell away. Two of the five days.
That's a beginning. How were those two nights?
Irritatingly, those were the nights I got to sleep quickest, so apparently it works. The rest of the week my mind was racing and I was still awake after two.
Anything. Had I locked the door, had I said something stupid at dinner, pointless things. When the lights go off I just worry round and round.
And if you compare the nights now to a fortnight ago?
They're better, honestly. It used to be every single night and now it's about half of them. I also swapped my phone for a novel before bed, and reading helps me wind down.
That's real progress. What do you want to do about the breathing this coming week?
Every night this week, five minutes, straight after brushing my teeth so it doesn't slip my mind.
Linking it to teeth-brushing is a good idea. I'll check in on it next time.
A couple of things, and neither is really about me. First, my mom rang on Sunday to say she and my dad might separate. They're trying it out, with him moving out for a while.
That's a lot to hear over the phone. How are you taking it?
It's strange. I can't say I'm shocked, because the two of them have had a cold marriage for years. The one I feel for is my younger brother. He still lives there and he's stuck in the middle.
He is. I've been phoning him more. A sixteen year old shouldn't be the referee.
A friend who lives down my hall. She drinks heavily now, basically nightly, and at a party last weekend she blacked out. It was me who got her home.
That's a lot to carry for her. Are you drinking at these parties as well?
No, I don't, I was sober that night. She's the one I'm concerned about. I'm not sure it's my place to bring it up with her.
That if I'm really her friend I should say something. I haven't figured out how yet.
We can work on that together when you're ready.
Next time, maybe. Mainly I needed to get both of these said.
Hello. You were going to tally your drinks every day after our last session. How did keeping track go?
I managed three days, Monday through Wednesday. After that I quit writing it down, because I hated seeing the numbers.
Three days still tells us something. What did you see?
Four beers a night, sometimes five. To be honest it's been a worse week than the ones before. I had got it down to two a night and it's climbed back.
Any sense of why it climbed?
I can't sleep. My head won't shut off, so I keep drinking until it does. And then I'm awake at four regardless, feeling awful.
So part of what the drinking does is get you to sleep.
More or less. It lets me avoid lying awake with my own thoughts.
Is anyone else helping you with the sleep?
My psychiatrist, I have an appointment on the twelfth. A month ago she started me on trazodone for sleeping. I skip it when I've been drinking though, since the two aren't supposed to be combined.
She'll want to know that. Would you take your three days of tallies along to the appointment?
Not sure. Possibly. I need to decide whether I want her seeing them.
